title: China Wind Power’s Global Challenge
gist: A paywalled teaser/abstract, not a full article: it argues Chinese wind turbine makers are dominant at home yet far less visible in export markets than Chinese solar, EV and battery firms, because domestic wind lacks the profit-destroying overcapacity that pushes other cleantech sectors abroad and because wind's project economics penalize short reliability records. The stated conclusion is that Chinese wind firms are nonetheless going abroad and should win in price-sensitive emerging markets.

themes.theme: Why wind lags China's other cleantech exports

insights.claim: Chinese wind turbine makers dominate their home market but are much less visible in export markets than Chinese solar, EV and battery companies.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Do not extrapolate the solar/EV/battery export-share playbook to Chinese wind equipment; the export ramp is a separate, slower story to underwrite.
insights.quote: Chinese wind turbine makers are champions at home but much less visible abroad than their peers in solar, EVs and batteries.

insights.claim: China's domestic wind industry does not carry as much profit-destroying excess capacity as other cleantech sectors, so turbine makers can still earn money at home and have less need to export.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Domestic wind margins are structurally healthier than the rest of Chinese cleantech, which supports home-market earnings but weakens the deflation-export impulse foreign incumbents fear.

themes.theme: Reliability records gate wind project economics

insights.claim: In wind, lower equipment prices are often not enough to overcome buyers' perception of weaker service quality and the higher financing costs that come with a shorter reliability record.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Cost of capital, not sticker price, is the competitive battleground in wind — watch for lenders accepting Chinese turbines as the real signal that share shift has begun.

insights.claim: The fast product cycles that give Chinese EV brands a competitive edge actively hurt turbine makers, because rapid model turnover prevents any single design from accumulating a long reliability track record.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A reusable screen for capital-goods exporters: where assets are financed over decades, iteration speed is a liability rather than a moat.

themes.theme: Emerging markets as the entry wedge

insights.claim: Chinese wind firms are increasingly looking abroad and are expected to do well specifically in price-sensitive emerging markets rather than in developed markets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Expect Chinese turbine share gains to show up first in EM tenders; Western turbine incumbents' developed-market pricing is less immediately at risk than headline export fears imply.
insights.quote: Chinese wind firms are increasingly looking abroad, and are set to do well in price-sensitive emerging markets.
